title: Throughput Covenant & Operational Remediation Framework for Dedicated Pools
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: define a customer-facing throughput covenant (SLA) for Dedicated GPU pools and pair it with precise error-budget math, an autoscaler interlock policy, and a contractual remediation ladder. Goal is to create language that is measurable, operationally enforceable, and minimizes unexpected customer/ops churn during capacity degradations.
background: Customers purchasing Dedicated capacity have asked for clearer, actionable throughput guarantees tied to both latency and sustained throughput. Prior PM artifacts (see attachments) focused on percentiles and credit calculations; this ticket consolidates those learnings into a single covenant that binds measurements, notice windows, and autoscaler behavior so that legal + ops can sign off together.
acceptance_criteria: SLA clause drafted with unambiguous metric definitions (units, windowing, cardinality)
Error budget calculation defined and validated against historical telemetry (last 6 months) for two customer archetypes: steady-state web-text generation and bursty batch embeddings
Autoscaler interlock rules specified so that behavior during sustained degradation is deterministic and documented in the contract
Operational playbook (oncall runbook) written and linked with escalation steps and credit computation examples
Legal approves contract language and Sales can present a templated covenant to customers
contract_text_snippet: Throughput Covenant (sample): 'Redwood Inference guarantees that a Customer's Dedicated Pool will sustain a minimum committed throughput measured as the 95th-percentile served tokens-per-second per-pool over rolling 1-hour windows (the "Committed Throughput"). If the Committed Throughput falls below the Customer's purchased entitlement for more than 3 non-overlapping 1-hour windows within a billing day, Redwood will provide credits according to the Remediation Ladder below. Measurement excludes scheduled maintenance and force-maintenances with >=24h notice.'
error_budget_definition: We define an error event as a 1-hour window where actual served throughput < entitlement. Error budget for a 30-day period is the allowed count of such windows before credits escalate. Example formula (string): 'monthly_error_budget = floor(0.02 * total_1h_windows_in_period * entitlement_scale_factor)'. For a 30-day month and entitlement_scale_factor 1.0, monthly_error_budget = floor(0.02 * 720) = 14 windows. Credits start at proportional service credits for first 5 windows and escalate to refunds/termination rights beyond defined thresholds.
remediation_ladder: Tier 1 (1-5 windows/month): 10% service credit to monthly fee; Tier 2 (6-14 windows/month): 30% credit + mandatory technical remediation plan within 5 business days; Tier 3 (>=15 windows/month): 60% credit and option for Customer to terminate with pro-rated refund. All credits computed net of taxes and capped at 100% of monthly Dedicated fee. Credits formula and notice language attached in appendix.
measurement_notes: Metric collection: use 'dedicated.pool_throughput.tokens_per_sec' aggregated at pool_id with 1-minute buckets, then compute rolling 1-hour sums. Exclude requests flagged with 'maintenance=true' or routed to failover pools. Clock sync requirement: all hosts must report in UTC; missing data >5% of minutes in a 1-hour window marks that window as 'insufficient data' and excluded from entitlement computations (unless SLA dispute is raised).
autoscaler_interlock_policy: When a pool's 1-hour throughput falls below 95% of entitlement for two consecutive 1-hour windows, autoscaler behaves as follows: (a) attempt emergency scale-up (if capacity available in reserved pool), (b) if scale-up not possible within 10 minutes, enter 'degraded mode' where new requests are diverted to best-effort fallback model variant with documented quality delta, (c) create incident and notify account owners per Notice Windows. The contract will reference these exact actions and clarify when credits apply (e.g., if degraded mode invoked due to capacity shortage credits start accruing at first qualifying 1-hour window).
operational_playbook: Runbook excerpt: 1) Threshold alert fires (95% entitlement sustained breach) → Pager to Dedicated SRE + Customer Success; 2) SRE attempts fast-scale via reserved capacity CLI (docs/link); 3) If fast-scale fails, enable degraded routing and record fallback model version; 4) Collect artifacts: pool telemetry snapshot, autoscaler decisions, internal reason codes; 5) Within 24h produce Post-Event Summary for the customer including credit computation draft; 6) If unresolved after 5 business days create remediation plan with milestones. Templates and dashboards linked in attachments.
decision_log: 2025-01-15: Decided to measure throughput on rolling 1-hour windows (Ava, Ethan, Priya) — trade-off: smoother noise vs slower detection for bursts
2025-01-21: Chose percentile-based committed throughput (95th) instead of median to make SLA resilient to short tail performance (legal and SRE consensus)
2025-01-28: Agreed autoscaler interlock will prioritize reserved capacity; if unavailable, fallback to degraded mode with documented quality impact (ops/infra)
2025-02-01: Legal requested explicit exclude-list for scheduled maintenance and agreed notice threshold of >=24 hours
progress_updates: 2025-01-13: Drafting initial formula for monthly_error_budget; pulled 6 months telemetry for two pilot customers (internal dataset)
2025-01-19: Ran simulation of credit accrual using last quarter telemetry — error budget calibration looks conservative for bursty embedding workloads
2025-01-25: Ops prototype of autoscaler interlock implemented in staging; observed 7-12min failover path for heavy contention cases
2025-02-04: Legal provided redline to sample contract text; awaiting final SRE sign-off on measurement exclusions

open_questions: Should we allow customers to purchase 'burst peaker' add-on to increase error budget during known campaign windows?
Do we include cross-region failover in entitlement calculations or treat it as separate best-effort capacity?
What is the acceptable dispute window for customers to contest computed credits? (suggest 30 days)
